newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends unchanged against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends unchanged against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed unchanged at 8.2951 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Thursday with strong pro-yuan sentiment balanced by fears of possible central bank intervention, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2956.

Dealers said pro-yuan sentiment remained strong after Beijing announced on Monday a foreign trade surplus of $6.71 billion in the first three months of the year, up 25.7 percent from the same period last year.
But many said they expected central bank intervention to keep the yuan below the key 8.2950 resistance level.
The yuan opened flat at 8.2951 and moved in a narrow range of 8.2950 and an intraday low of 8.2955 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2902 late in trading.
Trading was less active than Wednesday with most business done at about 8.2952, traders said.
One dealer said buying interest in the yuan was strong on market expectations of further rises in the short term.
"As a result of that, the yuan has closed just below the main 8.2950 resistance level every day recently."
"If the yuan fails to breach the level soon and with the impact of the trade surplus declining, the yuan could fall over the next few days," he added.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to close down on Friday.
The yuan closed down at 6.5991 from 6.5610 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at an intraday low of 1.0715 from 1.0714 against the Hong Kong dollar.
